asset_manifest.description: A professional-grade kit for splitting sedimentary layers to reveal compression fossils.

components.visual_details: Forged high-carbon steel with a 3-inch wide, tapered edge. The blade is extremely thin compared to a standard chisel. The handle features a rubberized 'safety grip' to protect the hand from stray hammer strikes.
components.wear_state: Slightly scuffed at the tip with silver metal showing through black powder coating.

components.visual_details: A 22oz pointed-tip rock hammer with a blue vinyl grip. The head is polished steel, showing a flat striking face on one side and a sharp 'pick' end on the other.
components.scale_reference: Hammer head is roughly 7 inches long.

asset_manifest.usage_pose: The chisel is held at a 45-degree angle to the shale layer, with the wide blade inserted into a visible crack. The hammer is captured mid-swing, ready to strike the flat end of the chisel.
asset_manifest.lighting: Sharp highlights on the polished steel edges to emphasize the 'new' and 'professional' quality of the grad student gear.
